title: Region-aware Evidence Automation Workbench: residency + retention proof pipelines
creator: Anika Patel
description: Build a region-aware evidence automation workbench that maps SOC 2 and ISO 27001 control requirements to concrete, verifiable artifacts and automates collectors, retention enforcement, and auditor-facing exports. The workbench will: (1) provide a control->collector mapping UI, (2) run scheduled collectors and ad-hoc on-demand collectors scoped by region/tenant, (3) store immutable evidence artifacts with region tagging and retention TTLs, (4) surface provenance and KMS-backed hashes for auditor verification, and (5) generate auditor-ready export bundles and a control coverage dashboard. This effort is meant to reduce manual evidence work in audits, support Private/VPC deployments with residency constraints, and be compatible with Dedicated and Hosted modes.
acceptance_criteria: Control mapping UI covers at least 80% of SOC 2 Common Criteria and mapped ISO 27001 clauses for core infra controls
At least 12 automated collectors implemented (e.g., RBAC config, config drift snapshots, KMS activity logs, SSO/SAML assertion logs, backup success/failure, retention-policy enforcement events)
Artifacts stored with region tag and immutable flag; retention TTLs enforced with test harness simulating legal hold and TTL expiry
Artifacts include signed SHA256 hash + KMS key identifier; verification flow to re-hash and validate signatures documented
Auditor export generates zipped bundle with manifest.json, per-control evidence pointers, and human-readable summary; export validated by internal audit team
Telemetry: missing-evidence alerts, collector health metrics, per-control coverage metric available in Console with ability to drill into failing artifacts
tasks: Design control->collector schema and JSON manifest format (PM + Eng + Security)
Prototype collector runner that supports region-scoped execution and identity delegation
Integrate with KMS for signing artifact hash (support AWS KMS and GCP KMS in first phase)
Implement immutable storage layer with WORM support and retention TTL enforcement
Add UI for mapping controls to collectors and per-tenant region override
Create auditor export generator, manifest format, and sample bundle
Add alerting rules for missing evidence windows and collector failures
Run EU region pilot with two customers and capture feedback
notes_and_decisions: 2025-01-12: Decided to standardize on a single artifact manifest format (flat JSON manifest) to simplify auditor parsing and minimize SDK churn.

2025-01-16: Trade-off: WORM storage will be implemented using object lock for Hosted; Dedicated/Private will provide guidance and an opt-in agent for local WORM. Reason: different deployments have different storage primitives.
2025-01-20: Chose KMS-signed hashes instead of a custom HSM-backed attestation for v1 to accelerate delivery; HSM path remains on roadmap for high-security customers.
2025-01-24: Collector runner will default to strong consistency for evidence writes; eventual-consistency collectors (analytics views) will be tagged to avoid being used as primary proof artifacts.
2025-01-29: Legal hold semantics: allow retention override with an explicit legal-hold flag and audit trail. Requires security review and legal sign-off before enabling cross-region holds.

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Evidence gaps during rollout could cause auditor confidence issues. Mitigation: run a shadow-collection mode and surface coverage gaps in Console before enabling export to auditors.
Risk: Regional legal holds could conflict with automated TTL enforcement. Mitigation: implement explicit, immutable legal-hold flags and admin approvals with audit logs.
Risk: Large artifact sizes for backup proofs. Mitigation: adopt pointer-based manifests with deduplicated blob store and optional on-demand retrieval for large binary artifacts.
